verdict: The Worldpay deal transformed Global Payments' scale — GAAP revenue jumped 64% — but over $1 billion of acquisition amortization and integration costs crushed GAAP operating profit.

segments.name: SMB
segments.note: Payment acceptance and software for small and medium-sized businesses — the largest channel.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.note: Payments for large global merchants, transformed by Worldpay.

segments.name: Platforms
segments.note: Software platforms and payment services sold through partners.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Other revenue lines outside the three main channels.

opex.name: Sales, general & admin
opex.note: Running the combined company, including $344M of acquisition, integration, separation and transformation costs excluded from adjusted results.

otherDetail: Interest and other expense of $242M, more than offset by $202M of income from discontinued operations (the Issuer Solutions business being sold) and a $67M income-tax benefit — a net $26M added to profit. Tax was a benefit this quarter, not a cost, so it is included here rather than as a tax charge.
follow100Note: Figures are rounded to the nearest $1 million from the release (revenue $3,306.3M, total net income $290.2M). Kept as profit is total net income, including $202M from discontinued operations; continuing operations earned $88M and $281M in total was attributable to Global Payments shareholders. Cost of service includes $755M of amortization of acquired intangibles from the Worldpay deal.

takeaways.title: Worldpay changed the company's size
takeaways.text: GAAP revenue rose 64% to $3.31 billion with Worldpay consolidated; on a normalized like-for-like basis, adjusted net revenue grew over 4% to $3.18 billion.

takeaways.title: GAAP operating profit was squeezed
takeaways.text: Operating income fell to $246 million because cost of service includes $763 million of acquisition-related amortization and adjustments, and SG&A includes $344 million of deal and transformation costs. Adjusted operating income was $1,353 million.

takeaways.title: Synergy target raised
takeaways.text: Management raised the expected annual run-rate Worldpay cost synergies to $650 million and kept 2026 guidance unchanged: adjusted EPS of $13.60-13.80.

oneTimers: GAAP results carry over $1.1 billion of Worldpay-related items: $763 million of adjustments in cost of service (mostly $755 million of acquired-intangible amortization) and $344 million in SG&A (acquisition/integration $222M, transformation $51M, employee termination $63M, other $8M).

Income from discontinued operations was $202 million, and the quarter's tax line was a $67 million benefit rather than a charge — both lift total net income of $290 million well above continuing-operations income of $88 million.
